name: Luz Dean
life: “I still remember a grocer keeping my little girl's bag behind the oranges.” Saturday often includes a stop at Tideline Market, where Luz picks out the bruised fruit first and asks the seller what will ripen by supper.
voice: I wrote the name of the grocer who holds my daughter's school bag when my watch runs late.
appearance: Luz has an aquiline nose and a square chin. Look for a center part and straight chestnut hair. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a long navy raincoat with a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. In conversation Luz holds eye contact until the other person has finished.
personality: Luz talks very little about private fear and recognizes it quickly in strangers. Offering a choice of seats is one of Luz's ways of saying that it is all right to leave.
agenda: To thank the grocer for protecting the school bag.
family: Sam Lim is Luz’s stepsibling. Luz asks what the birthday guest would like this year. Sam remembers the birthdays. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *A doctor moves away*, Sam says, “I am the young physician replacing her. My first week's schedule is full of people who want to say goodbye.”
connections: Marc Carr (neighbor). A watch worker thanks the person who knows which child's school bag stays behind the orange boxes.

reactions.situation: A colleague leaves a name off the thank-you wall
reactions.response: Luz allows a private thank-you to stay private even on unveiling day.

reactions.situation: A diner goes silent in the middle of a noisy family celebration
reactions.response: Luz takes a small plate to the quieter end of the table and saves the seat beside it.

reactions.situation: When pressed to explain someone else's silence
reactions.response: Luz says only what happened and lets the absent person keep their reasons.
